_readme: Every knob the agent obeys. Copy to settings.json (setup.sh does this for you) and edit. Full docs: README.md#settings.

run._daily_note: Target N STRONG applications per calendar day; hard ceiling max_applications_per_day, counted from logs/applications-log.md entries dated today (SUBMITTED only). The target is a goal, never a reason to lower the fit bar: when strong matches run out, stop for the day, even at 0. 0 means no target / no daily ceiling.
run._lifetime_cap_note: Hard ceiling on TOTAL applications ever sent to one company, counted across applications/ AND logs/applications-log.md. An ATS dedupes by email, so every req lands on one candidate profile: many reqs in a short window read as spray, not interest, and buy nothing past the second. At the cap, SKIP the company and log one line.
run._interview_pause_note: Never send a new application to a company where an interview is in progress. A second recruiter can auto-reject the new req, stamping a rejection on the profile of an active loop. List interviewing companies in targets.skip_companies with the reason.
run._interview_tracker_note: Optional absolute path to a note or file where YOU track interviews, OAs and recruiter threads (any format; company names are grepped). When set, the agent reads it at the start of every run and treats every company named in it as a HARD SKIP, on top of skip_companies. Keep it current and you never have to edit skip_companies by hand. Empty means off.

schedule._frequency_options: manual | hourly | every-2-hours | every-3-hours | every-6-hours | daily | weekdays

targets._linkedin_location_overrides_note: Optional, kept private here because settings.json is gitignored: replace or add LinkedIn search centers for scripts/linkedin_sweep.py, e.g. {"Western Wisconsin": {"location": "Eau Claire, Wisconsin, United States", "distance": 25}}. Keys are targets.locations entries; values take location, distance (miles: 5/10/25/50/75/100) and remote (true/false). Wisconsin searches are capped at 25 miles (no relocation).
targets._min_annual_comp_note: Applies to FULL-TIME roles only. Internships post hourly or monthly pay and would fail an annual floor, so they are judged by internship_min_hourly_usd instead.
targets._internship_note: Hourly floor for internships. 0 means no floor: judge internships by prestige_note alone. Top US SWE internships run roughly $40-$120/hour.
targets.prestige_note: One or two sentences describing what makes a company worth your time. The agent uses this as a judgment gate when a posting lists no salary band. Example: 'Only frontier AI labs, top-tier AI startups, or top quant firms. Skip ordinary enterprise software companies.'
targets._platform_focus_skip_note: Platform/stack requirements you do not target (e.g. a mobile or OS ecosystem). A role where one is a CORE responsibility is skipped; the only exception is an explicitly cross-platform role whose majority of actual work strongly matches strongest_stack. Generic overlap (one shared language) does not rescue it. The employer's product line alone is never a reason to skip. sourcing_priority orders searches; it is not a filter.
targets._company_rules_note: Per-company overrides, e.g. {"Acme": {"routine_sourcing": false, "consider_only_if": ["..."]}}. routine_sourcing false = never query that board as a sourcing step.
skip_notes: Defense and ITAR employers require US persons.
Companies that do not sponsor visas are a dead end if you need sponsorship.

sourcing._note: broad_sweeps false: do not run delta_sweep.py, portal_sweep.py or multi-page scans as a matter of course; source one employer board or one narrow search at a time and stop at the first strong match. rotate_methods: do not repeat the same search method back to back within a day; rotate between employer career pages / verified ATS boards (preferred), the sweep scripts, narrow LinkedIn searches, and Indeed (source only). Record the method used in state/status.md so the next run picks a different one.

discovery_sources.name: LinkedIn
discovery_sources.how: scripts/linkedin_sweep.py or one public guest search page

discovery_sources.name: Indeed
discovery_sources.how: Indeed connector or one narrow search page

discovery_sources.name: Glassdoor
discovery_sources.how: one narrow single-page Glassdoor job search

sourcing._discovery_sources_note: Job sites used ONLY to find leads, never to apply. Remove an entry to stop using that site, or add one with name/how/never_use. Every lead is verified on the employer's own career page or ATS posting before applying; third-party remote, location, salary, experience and employment-type labels are never trusted. Sources rotate with equal consideration, and the same company + title (+ req) across sources is one lead. salary_estimates_are_not_posted_comp: true marks a site whose salary figures are estimates; they may be logged as context, comp gates use the employer-posted range.
sourcing._cooldowns_note: Source backoff, recorded in the 'Source cooldowns' table at the top of state/status.md with the date. invalid_source_days: an exact board URL/slug confirmed invalid is not retried for this long. no_match_board_days: a valid board with zero matching roles is not routinely rechecked for this long. bad_leads_before_switch: consecutive bad/duplicate/stale/mislabeled leads from one method or discovery source before switching immediately (tracked per source). An exhausted source is never retried in the same run; an early recheck is allowed only when another method surfaces a specific new job URL from that company.

channels._why: Aggregators need accounts and hide the real form. The agent applies on the company's own ATS only.
channels._signed_in_portals_note: Optional. Career portals where YOU created the account and your Chrome is signed in. The agent may apply inside that session. It never creates accounts or types passwords; a login page is NEEDS HUMAN.

broker._broker_note: Optional. scripts/code_broker.py reads emailed verification codes over Gmail IMAP and pastes them into the page without the agent ever seeing the code or the password. One-time setup, done by YOU, not the agent: turn on 2-Step Verification, create an app password at https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords, then in your own Terminal run `security add-generic-password -s jobapply-gmail-imap -a <gmail_account> -w` and paste it at the hidden prompt. Check with `python3 scripts/code_broker.py check`. signup_email_pattern is the plus address used per portal, {tag} = portal name.

integrations._post_run_note: Optional path to a python3 script run after each run. Left empty by default.
